methodological_rigor.justification: This is a well-executed single-centre retrospective cohort study (n=910, 2014-2021, IRCCS IRST, Italy) with manual review of unstructured EHR data and an algorithmically derived line-of-therapy definition validated in prior publications. Kaplan-Meier methods are appropriate for the descriptive survival objectives. However, the study is explicitly descriptive without multivariable survival analyses—survival outcomes are not statistically tested or adjusted for confounders, which is a stated limitation that precludes causal inference. The exclusion of clinical trial patients may introduce selection bias. No formal statistical comparisons between treatment arms are presented; comparisons are qualitative.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: This is a single-centre retrospective descriptive cohort (Oxford LoE 4). The study documents real-world patterns of ICI and targeted therapy uptake in Italy between 2014-2021 and demonstrates improved survival coinciding with immunotherapy availability. While this provides useful contextual data for health system benchmarking and policy, it does not test any specific clinical hypothesis. The confirmatory nature of the findings (ICI and targeted therapy benefit largely consistent with trial data) limits its direct clinical impact beyond the Italian setting, though the inclusion of patients with PS≥2 excluded from trials adds some representational value.

reporting_quality.justification: The manuscript follows STROBE-compliant reporting: eligibility criteria, data sources, variable definitions, statistical methods, and limitations are all clearly described. The line-of-therapy algorithm references a prior publication for methodological transparency. Sankey diagrams aid treatment sequencing visualization. Eleven explicit limitations are enumerated, including data masking protocols, the exclusion of trial patients, algorithmic misclassification risk, and COVID-19 effects on 2020-2021 outcomes. EHR data from a single licensed Italian centre are not publicly deposited, which is standard for hospital-based datasets; no code sharing is mentioned.

novelty_literature.justification: The rapid uptake of ICI therapy and corresponding improvement in NSCLC survival from 2018 onwards is well-documented in multiple published real-world studies from Canada, Germany, Sweden, Denmark, and the UK cited in the manuscript. The Italian single-centre setting provides geographic specificity and extends prior work by Danesi et al. from the same institution, but offers limited new conceptual insights. The treatment and survival trends are broadly confirmatory rather than hypothesis-generating. The comparison of de novo versus recurrent disease is the most informative subgroup analysis, though this distinction is also described in prior literature.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is clearly organized, with well-defined objectives, transparent methods, and a comprehensive discussion that contextualizes Italian findings within the international real-world evidence landscape. The temporal trends in treatment uptake and survival are well-presented. The 11-point limitations section is unusually thorough and reflects appropriate epistemic caution. Sankey diagram visualization of treatment sequences is a useful presentational strength. Some repetition between abstract, results, and discussion sections is minor. The conclusion appropriately avoids over-interpretation of descriptive findings.

key_strengths: Large single-centre real-world cohort (n=910, 8-year accrual) with manual EHR review achieving high data completeness including PS, biomarker testing, and treatment sequencing
Temporal analysis captures the full pre- and post-immunotherapy transition period in Italy, providing policy-relevant data on ICI uptake timelines and survival impact
Inclusion of patients with ECOG PS≥2 excluded from clinical trials broadens real-world applicability
Comprehensive 11-item limitations section demonstrates appropriate epistemic caution for a descriptive study
key_concerns: Purely descriptive design without multivariable survival analysis precludes adjustment for confounders and limits causal interpretation of survival trends
Single-centre design limits generalizability to other Italian or European cancer centres with different resources, patient mix, and approval timelines
Exclusion of clinical trial participants introduces selection bias and may systematically undercount early ICI exposure
Core findings (ICI uptake and associated survival improvement post-2018) are substantially confirmatory of multiple prior international real-world studies, limiting novelty
chief_reviewer.rationale: A competently executed descriptive real-world cohort study documenting Italian NSCLC treatment patterns and survival evolution over 2014-2021; the single-centre design, absence of adjusted survival analyses, and largely confirmatory findings position this as tier 3 publication requiring minor revisions primarily to emphasize its incremental geographic contribution and avoid overstating survival-treatment causal claims.
